risks.risk: Italian CCNL labour contracts vary by region and role, making rule encoding complex.
risks.mitigation: Partner with Italian labour consultants and encode rules incrementally by contract type.

risks.risk: Low digital adoption among independent restaurateurs slows onboarding.
risks.mitigation: Provide white-glove migration, mobile-first UI, and Italian-language support.

risks.risk: Forecasting requires historical POS data that customers may not share or have.
risks.mitigation: Seed models with public weather/event data and allow manual calibration until sufficient history accumulates.

risks.risk: Established scheduling SaaS enter Italy with localized compliance.
risks.mitigation: Own the Italian compliance niche first and build switching costs through payroll/POS integration.

risks.risk: Fragmented Italian POS ecosystem makes integration costly.
risks.mitigation: Start with CSV import and manual data entry; prioritize integrations only after paying pilot customers.

risks.risk: Seasonal restaurant closures cause churn and revenue volatility.

investor_questions: How will you encode and stay current with the regional variations in Italian CCNL labour contracts?
What is your customer acquisition strategy for reaching thousands of fragmented independent restaurants in Italy?
Which Italian POS and payroll systems will you integrate with first, and what is the build timeline?
How accurate can cover forecasts be during the cold-start phase before you have customer POS history?
What prevents a larger scheduling platform from localizing for Italy and outspending you on CAC?
validation_experiments: Conduct 10 discovery interviews with independent restaurant and bar managers in Milan and Rome to validate scheduling pain and willingness to pay.
Launch an Italian-language landing page and drive targeted Meta ads to independent restaurateurs to measure email signup conversion.
Offer a free manual labour-cost audit to five restaurants using their historical rota data to quantify potential savings.
Post in Italian hospitality owner Facebook groups and forums to gauge interest and collect pre-launch waitlist signups.
Run a concierge MVP: manually build AI-style rotas for two to three restaurants using their bookings and weather data, then measure time saved versus their current process.

memo:
## Summary
ShiftPilot is an AI staff scheduling SaaS for independent restaurants and bars with 5–40 staff, launching in Italy before expanding to Southern Europe. It forecasts covers from bookings, weather, and local events, then builds rotas that respect Italian labour contracts (CCNL), targeting reduced overstaffing and last-minute gaps. Business model is subscription (SaaS). VentureLens score: 6.1 / 10; verdict: Promising: validate the key assumptions.

## Opportunity
Target customers are independent restaurants and bars with 5–40 staff in Italy, expanding to Southern Europe. Bottom-up market sizing: TAM €284.4M, SAM €71.1M, SOM €2.1M. Problem urgency is 7.5/10: scheduling is a weekly, time-consuming pain for thin-margin restaurateurs, though rarely an existential daily crisis. Competitive position is 6.0/10: established scheduling tools exist, but none dominate Italy with AI cover forecasting and CCNL-specific compliance. Direct competitors include 7shifts, Deputy, Sling, and Fourth (HotSchedules); Excel and paper rotas remain the incumbent substitute.

## Business model and unit economics
Revenue per customer per month: €79. Gross margin: 80%. Customer acquisition cost: €450. Monthly churn: 2.5%. Customer lifetime value (LTV): €2.5k. LTV to CAC: 5.6×. CAC payback: 7.1 months. Defensibility is 5.5/10: proprietary forecasting data and integration switching costs build over time, but there are no strong network effects. Execution feasibility is 5.0/10: combining AI forecasting, Italian labour-rule encoding, and POS integrations is demanding for a small seed team.

## Financial outlook
Fixed costs per month at launch: €22k. Starting cash: €400k. Projection horizon: 36 months. Sustained break-even: Not within 36 months. Extra funding needed to stay cash-positive: €408k. Customers at end of horizon: 2,850. Annual recurring revenue at end of horizon: €2.7M.

## Key risks
- Italian CCNL labour contracts vary by region and role, making rule encoding complex (high severity).
- Established scheduling SaaS enter Italy with localized compliance (high severity).
- Low digital adoption among independent restaurateurs slows onboarding (medium).
- Forecasting requires historical POS data that customers may not share or have (medium).
- Fragmented Italian POS ecosystem makes integration costly (medium).
- Seasonal restaurant closures cause churn and revenue volatility (medium).

Suggested mitigations include partnering with Italian labour consultants, owning the Italian compliance niche first, white-glove migration with mobile-first UI and Italian-language support, seeding models with public weather/event data, starting with CSV import, and offering seasonal pause pricing.

## Recommendation
Proceed with a seed investment conditional on validating key assumptions. Priorit
